 We are committed to giving our employees a flexible and connected way of working. A flexible and connected ZS allows us to combine work from home and on-site presence at clients/ZS offices for the majority of our week. The magic of ZS culture and innovation thrives in both planned and spontaneous face-to-face connections.

 Travel is a requirement at ZS for client facing ZSers; business needs of your project and client are the priority. While some projects may be local, all client-facing ZSers should be prepared to travel as needed. jd_text:
Description 
 About Alvarez & Marsal 
 Alvarez & Marsal (A&M) is a global consulting firm with over 10,000 entrepreneurial, action and results-oriented professionals in over 40 countries. We take a hands-on approach to solving our clients' problems and assisting them in reaching their potential. Our culture celebrates independent thinkers and doers who positively impact our clients and shape our industry. The collaborative environment and engaging work—guided by A&M's core values of Integrity, Quality, Objectivity, Fun, Personal Reward, and Inclusive Diversity—are why our people love working at A&M.
 The Team 
 The A&M Global Transaction Advisory Group (“GTAG”) is comprised of former Big Four CPAs and CAs who provide private equity and corporate clients buy side and sell side financial accounting due diligence. GTAG professionals actively engage in assessing a target’s quality of earnings, analyzing cash flows, reviewing working capital, identifying key business drivers, reviewing forecasts, and conducting comprehensive discussions with management and their advisors. GTAG professionals routinely team with the firm’s operational, tax, commercial, and information technology professionals to deliver a truly integrated solution to clients.
 How you will contribute 
- Assist with core financial due diligence, helping to identify key risks and potential deal breakers, assess the strengths and weaknesses of the business against industry benchmarks, and assist with the evaluation of the potential transaction in the context of their clients’ investment strategy.
- Analyse detailed financial statement information including income statement, balance sheet, cash flow and key operational data. Synthesize and convert the data into meaningful information that is used to drive discussions with target management and drive observations and conclusions.
- Assess the quality of the target company's reported earnings, net assets and cash flows.
- After an investigative analysis, assist in the construction of deal-oriented reports and presentations for clients that highlight the key financial, commercial and other findings facing investments and the drivers behind maintainable profits and cash flows. Assist the team in further articulating how such findings should be incorporated into the client's valuation and sale / purchase agreement and provide other negotiating points.
- Participate in meetings and conference calls with target company management and with client personnel and will serve as an additional point of contact for client personnel with respect to day-to-day execution matters.

jd_text:
Who We Are 
FTI Consulting is the leading global expert firm for organizations facing crisis and transformation. We work with many of the world’s top multinational corporations, law firms, banks and private equity firms on their most important issues to deliver impact that makes a difference. From resolving disputes, navigating crises, managing risk and optimizing performance, our teams respond rapidly to dynamic and complex situations.
At FTI Consulting, you’ll work side-by side with leaders who have shaped history, helping solve the biggest challenges making headlines today. From day one, you’ll be an integral part of a focused team where you can make a real impact. You’ll be surrounded by an open, collaborative culture that embraces diversity, recognition, professional development and, most importantly, you.
Are you ready to make your impact?
 About The Role
FTI Technology’s Blockchain and Digital Assets practice is experiencing exponential growth amid blockchain and digital asset technology innovation and we are currently looking for a dynamic, highly energized, and knowledgeable blockchain and/or digital assets Senior Consultant to add to our growing practice. This role is responsible for engaging in the delivery of complex blockchain and digital assets engagements.
Our Blockchain and Digital Assets practice provides a full range of services across the blockchain and digital assets sectors. Services include bankruptcy and restructuring, M&A due diligence, investigations, strategy and innovation, blockchain as a Service (BaaS), and more. Not only will you become a part of the FTI team, but you will also have a role on the teams of our clients. You will communicate the results of detailed analyses, refine litigation and business strategies, and work on a variety of other custom consulting projects. Our Senior Consultant position offers excellent opportunities and development for an entrepreneurial and intellectually curious experienced hire.
 What You’ll Do
- Execute technical investigations including blockchain analytics, fund flow tracing and data analysis — with structured upskilling in crypto analytics tools. 
- Review Smartcontracts and Blockchain platforms. 
- Support delivery of Risk Framework and Due Diligence mandates with quality-controlled outputs. 
- Prepare client-ready reports, expert summaries and analytical workpapers. 
- Conduct market and regulatory research to support pitch and proposal preparation. 
- Maintain and build knowledge of blockchain tools, analytics platforms and emerging protocols. 
- Support proposal writing and business development materials. 
- Support client engagement teams, work with a wide variety of clients to deliver professional services, investigative services, expert reports, and support business development activities at a strategic and tactical level. 
- Translate client requirements into formal agreements, establishing specific solutions/workflows, and lead the efforts that culminate in client acceptance of the results. 
- Assist in the development of each clients blockchain and/or digital assets solutions, excel at project consulting and management, deliver high quality work, and achieve outstanding results. 
- Contribute to contractual cost estimation, budget adherence, schedule creation, timeline management, and other deliverables. 
- Work closely with leadership to significantly contribute to thought-leadership initiatives, go to market strategies, sales efforts, and other practice development activities. 
- Support practice and business development initiatives, including expanding on client relationships. 
- Provide project management and support to team leads and clients. 
- Deliver daily updates of projects engagements to team leads. 
- Respond to client requests and setting clear expectations to internal and external stakeholders. 
 How You’ll Grow
We are committed to investing and supporting you in your professional development and we have developed a range of programs focused on fostering leadership, growth and development opportunities. We aim to promote continuous learning and individual skills development through on-the-job learning, self-guided professional development courses and certifications. You’ll be assigned a dedicated coach to mentor, guide and support you through regular coaching sessions and serve as an advocate for your professional growth. As you progress through your career at FTI Consulting, we offer tailored programs for critical professional milestones to ensure you are prepared and empowered to take on your next role.
 What You Will Need to Succeed
 Basic Qualifications 
- Bachelor’s Degree 
- Experience in consulting, data analytics, business intelligence, investigative research, or something else we aren’t thinking of. The general areas of focus for the practice are blockchain technology, crypto assets, DeFi, CeFi and NFTs. A strong interest in these areas would be helpful 
- Experience in code review 
- Advanced communication skills with the ability to influence across all levels internally and externally 
- This role requires travel to clients and FTI offices 
- Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis; this position does not provide visa sponsorship 
 Preferred Qualifications
- Possess strong quantitative and qualitative research and analytical skills 
- You are naturally curious. You ask meaningful, thoughtful questions, listen carefully, and are eager to begin the problem-solving process once you have the information you need 
- Possess strong team-oriented personality characteristics: hard-working, thoughtful, and collaborative, with a positive outlook and confidence 
- Able to adapt quickly in handling multiple/evolving tasks as a result of new engagements and/or re-prioritized deadlines 
- Highly motivated, eager to learn, willing to travel, and able to motivate others 
- Able to utilize technology to solve complex problems 
- Relevant experience in digital assets is preferred, but a deep personal interest or a passion for learning about blockchain technology and the digital asset industry is welcome. 
- Programming skills are a plus: Python, R, SQL, Solidity, Go, Rust. 
- Outstanding at written and speaking skills; must be able to create status reports, write official reports, forensic reports, and demonstrate an ability to convey the complexity of blockchain and digital assets in easy-to-understand ways. 
- Experience in contributing to high-performing teams in an accelerated growth environment. 
- Well-developed analytical skills and the ability to provide clarity to complex issues and synthesize large amounts of information. 
- Blockchain forensics a plus, including experience with CipherTrace, Chainalysis, TRM Labs, or equivalent.

We Do Consulting Differently 
 BRG’s Financial Institution Advisory practice specializes in helping commercial banks, consumer finance companies, credit unions, mortgage banks, capital market participants and insurance companies solve pressing complex business issues. The group brings a mix of functional experts—including CPAs, CFAs, CROs, CRCMs, FRMs, former regulators, financial modelers, technologists, former bankers, and longtime consultants—to address immediate risks and drive tangible benefits.
 The team of experts are looking for a highly energetic, junior level CPA, with 2 to 6 years of experience, who is eager to take their public accounting audit experience to the next level. Rather than auditing, you will be doing a variety of more challenging work such as analyzing financial statements, helping clients implement new accounting standards, performing investigations into accounting policies / practices, and addressing whether audit procedures were executed sufficiently. Other assignments include helping clients implement new accounting and risk systems and assisting financial institutions in executing transactions including portfolio acquisitions, mergers and spin-offs. The work will be varied and high paced such that you will get a broad array of experience that you may not be exposed to at the Big 4 or other large accounting firms. 
 The ideal candidate is a licensed CPA (or has passed multiple exam sections) with hands-on experience executing SEC registrant audits at a large public accounting firm. We highly prefer candidates who bring a solid baseline knowledge of financial instruments and possess direct audit experience within the financial services sector, specifically with banks, fintechs, broker-dealers, REITs, investment management firms, or insurance companies.
 BRG is high-end boutique consulting firm that works for premier global institutions, regulators and also serves in an expert witness role in some of the most contentious accounting and auditing litigation. The Financial Institution Advisory group is small enough that you will immediately feel comfortable in the group but big enough to work on some of the most high-profile matters impacting the financial services world. 
 Responsibilities 
- Work directly with senior professionals (many of whom are former Big 4) to execute various financial institution advisory projects related to accounting, auditing, financial analysis. Unlike the Big 4 you will also have the opportunity to work on financial risk management engagements including credit risk, valuation, capital planning, and stress-testing, liquidity, resolution planning, and model risk management. Functional areas of work encompass accounting, auditing, SEC reporting, regulatory, risk and controls; finance and accounting; technology enablement; and business process optimization. 
- Work on data / document intensive projects, including analytics, controls, governance, and financial analysis, to support a variety of different engagements. 
- Plan and manage all aspects or certain aspects of client engagements depending on their size and complexity. 
- Delegate assignments to staff, instruct and monitor progress, and review work product for completeness and accuracy. 
- Develop analyses and client ready work product that demonstrates insights in to the key risks or roadblocks related to the matter. 
- Establish controls and procedures to ensure the accuracy of analyses and conclusions. 
- Manage client relationships and communicate results and work products as appropriate. 
- Demonstrate creativity and efficient use of relevant software tools, analytical methods and computer models to develop solutions. 
- Participate in group practice meetings, contribute to business development initiatives and office functions such as staff training and recruiting. 
- Prioritize assignments and responsibilities in order to meet goals and deadlines.
 Financial Industry / Product Knowledge 
 Some foundational knowledge related to the any of the below areas is preferred:
- Banking (community / regional / money center / international / international branch) 
- Mortgage (originators, servicers, secondary marketing, GSEs) 
- Auto Finance 
- Student Loans 
- Commercial Loans (including commercial real estate) 
- Other consumer finance 
- Equipment Finance 
- Deposits 
- Capital Markets (securitization, prime broker, equity / debt issuance) 
- Derivatives 
- Structured Products 
- Insurance 
- Capital Planning 
- Liquidity Planning 
 Functional Capabilities 
 Prior experience of the following topical areas is highly preferred:
- Auditing 
- SEC filings and disclosures 
- Control testing 
- Risk and Control Assessments. 
- Process mapping/flows. 
- Business process / control remediation. 
- Business analysts (user requirement development / user acceptance testing); 
- Credit risk management. 
- Financial risk management. 
- Quantitative analytics. 
- Valuation of financial instruments. 
- Project / program managers. 
- RPA, current knowledge of AI used for segmentation, pricing/complaint analysis. 
 Basic Qualifications 
- Master’s degree or equivalent in accounting, finance, or a related field; alternatively, completion of a five-year accelerated accounting program, or a combined bachelor's and master's degree is highly preferred. 
- Minimum two to four (2-4) years of relevant experience in an accounting or Big Four consulting firm, specializing in audit, forensics, or dispute and damages matters. 
- Certified Public Accountant (CPA) designation, or documented progress toward obtaining the CPA, is important for long-term career advancement. 
- Demonstrated proficiency with Excel and other Microsoft Office applications. 
- Thorough grasp of accounting principles and financial statements, such as GAAP, along with understanding how debits and credits relate to the statement of cash flow, income statement, balance sheet, and trial balance. 
- Prior work experience with a focus on financial services in a consulting environment preferred. 
- Strong PowerPoint presentation skills/techniques. Ability to create decks and agendas that provide robust transparency as to project status. 
- Proven capability with MS Excel. A desire to expand those capabilities is required, as is the ability to train others to use such tools. 
- Desire and ability to manage processes and other more junior staff, as necessary. 
- Commitment to producing high quality analyses and attention to details.

- Strong verbal and written communication skills; and 
- Desire to work within a team environment. 
- Ability to travel to client sites on demand is required.

 Our Advisory team provide a wide variety of services that deliver value-led advice and outcomes. They have an in-depth knowledge of business, industry sectors and markets and understand the constantly changing risks and opportunities at the heart of our clients’ affairs. The team work across strategy, operations and improvement as well as at a transactional and defined project level. From technology to risk advisory, they’re experts in following through on top-level instructions and resolving the finer details – all in one straight-forward package. When you join them, you’ll work on some of the world's most exciting financial operations and business deals, building your experience and expertise alongside the brightest minds in the industry. 
 We’ll help you succeed 
 Leading organisations trust us because of the quality of our advice. That quality grows from a thorough understanding of their business, and that understanding comes from working closely with them and building long-lasting relationships. 
 You’ll be someone who is both comfortable working pro-actively and managing your own tasks, as well as confident collaborating with others and communicating regularly with senior managers, directors, and BDO’s partners to help businesses effectively. You’ll be encouraged to identify and draw attention to opportunities for enhancing our delivery and providing additional services to organisations we work with. . 
As a Senior Analyst or Analyst you'll join our Tech, Risk & Governance team (TRG) part of our Digital practice withing Consulting. This is a rapidly growing business area. You'll help clients understand and manage the risks arising from technology, transformation and digital change. The client base is diverse and you'll support technology risk assessments, IT internal audits, controls assurance and advisory engagements that strengthen governance, resilience and confidence in our clients most critical systems. This is an excellent opportunity to join a high performing digital team and develop your career.
 You'll be someone with: 
- Experience in technology risk, IT internal audit, IT assurance, risk and controls, or a closely related discipline, gained in professional services, financial services or another regulated organisation. 
- Experience in one or more relevant areas: IT general controls and SOX/ICFR; cloud risk; DevOps and SDLC controls; ERP risk and controls; operational resilience; third-party technology risk; data or AI governance; end-user computing; programme assurance 
- Financial services experience is desirable such as banks. insurers, asset managers, payments or capital markets organisations and frameworks such as FCA and PRA requirements, operational resilience and outsourcing or third-party risk expectations. 
- A practical understanding of technology risks and controls, with the ability to analyse evidence, identify control weaknesses and communicate their business impact clearly. 
- Relevant qualifications or progress towards them, such as CISA, ACA, ACCA, CIA, CRISC, CISSP or cloud certifications, would be advantageous but are not essential. 
 You’ll also be able to be yourself; we’ll recognise and value you for who you are and celebrate and reward your contributions to the business. We’re committed to agile working, and we offer everyone the opportunity to work in ways that suit them, their teams, and the task in hand.
 At BDO, we’ll help you achieve your personal goals and career ambitions, and we have programmes, resources, and frameworks that provide clarity and structure around career development.
 We’re in it together 
 Mutual support and respect is one of BDO’s core values and we’re proud of our distinctive, people-centred culture. From informal success conversations to formal mentoring and coaching, we’ll support you at every stage in your career, whatever your personal and professional needs.
 Our agile working framework helps us stay connected, bringing teams together where and when it counts so they can share ideas and help one another. At BDO, you’ll always have access to the people and resources you need to do your best work.
 We know that collaboration is the key to creating value for the companies we work with and satisfying experiences for our colleagues, so we’ve invested in state-of-the-art collaboration spaces in our offices. BDO’s people represent a wealth of knowledge and expertise, and we’ll encourage you to build your network, work alongside others, and share your skills and experiences. With a range of multidisciplinary events and dedicated resources, you’ll never stop learning at BDO.
 We’re looking forward to the future

WTW is seeking a highly analytical and technically skilled individual to join our Risk & Analytics team as a Physical Climate & Natural Catastrophe Risk Consultant. This role is ideal for candidates with a strong background in engineering, science, or analytics who are passionate about applying their expertise to real-world climate and catastrophe risk challenges.
 You will work alongside a multidisciplinary team of experts in insurance, science, and engineering to deliver cutting-edge risk assessments and consulting services to corporate clients across the U.S. and globally. This position offers the opportunity to contribute to innovative projects that span industries and geographies, with a focus on catastrophe risk engineering and climate resilience.
 The primary objectives are to support the Risk & Analytics team in advancing the catastrophe and climate risk management business in the US (primary focus) and globally. This includes providing assessments focused on catastrophe risk engineering, as well as leveraging RMS (Risk Management Solutions) models and other recognized catastrophe risk models in the insurance market, specifically for consulting projects delivered to WTW’s corporate clients. 
 We are open to hiring at a more junior level depending on the candidate’s experience.
 Note: visa employment-based non-immigrant visa sponsorship and/or assistance is not offered for this specific job opportunity.
 The Role 
- Conduct catastrophe risk engineering assessments and modeling analyses for corporate clients.
- Utilize and interpret outputs from catastrophe models (e.g., RMS, AIR, RQE, KatRisk).
- Support innovation in risk assessment where standard models or tools are unavailable.
- Evaluate property insurance portfolios and support climate-related financial disclosures across diverse asset types, including operational and construction-phase projects.
- Prepare technical reports and presentations to support insurance and risk decisions.
- Present findings to internal stakeholders and external clients.
- Perform data quality checks, hazard exposure analyses, and probabilistic modeling, ensuring results are robust and well-understood.
- Assist in business development, create proposals, and outline scope of work documents.
 -
 The Requirements 
- Strong academic background in engineering preferred (mechanical, civil, or structural preferred), science, mathematics, or a related field are also relevant.
- Solid understanding of catastrophe and probabilistic modeling principles.
- Experience with catastrophe risk engineering, including Probable Maximum Loss (PML) assessments and risk mitigation strategies.
- Proficiency with catastrophe modeling platforms such as RMS, AIR, RQE, or KatRisk.
- Familiarity with data analysis tools and languages such as SQL, R, and GIS.
- Experience in the insurance industry and understanding of policy structures is a plus.
- Ability to communicate complex technical and financial concepts to non-technical audiences.
- Strong leadership, presentation, and business development skills. 
 This position will remain posted for a minimum of three business days from the date posted or until sufficient/appropriate candidate slate has been identified.
 Compensation and Benefits 
 Base salary range and benefits information for this position are being included in accordance with requirements of various state/local pay transparency legislation. Please note that salaries may vary for different individuals in the same role based on several factors, including but not limited to location of the role, individual competencies, education/professional certifications, qualifications/experience, performance in the role and potential for revenue generation (Producer roles only).
 Compensation

 This role is also eligible for an annual short-term incentive bonus.

- Retirement Benefits: Qualified contributory pension plan (if eligible) and 401(k) plan with annual nonelective company contribution. Non-qualified retirement plans available to senior level colleagues who satisfy the plans’ eligibility requirements.

This role will be focused on managing and delivering large, strategic client engagements to multinational clients concerning their health and risk benefits globally. There may be a need to travel as needed for client and internal business needs. 
 Operating in the global marketplace means multinational companies face a variety of different business, cultural, language and regulatory environments. Our IGS line of business helps these companies navigate the challenges of multi-country complexity based on context knowledge of trends and innovative multi-client solutions. In particular, we help multinational companies develop global/cross-border solutions that meet the needs of both local and headquarter management in the design, establishment, financing, operation, oversight and monitoring of their compensation and benefit programs around the world. In doing so, we work closely with our local offices in other geographies, as well as subject matter experts in other segments. 
 Our Global Benefits Management (GBM) business has a particular focus around the coordination of insured employee benefits, and also has the breadth to consider other Benefits and Total Reward aspects as demanded by our clients. The GBM business is one of the fastest growing areas of our business with an expanding marketplace and exciting, evolving client needs. As an Associate Manager in our GBM delivery team, you will play a key part in this growth story, taking a lead role in delivering across multiple focus areas and geographies to some of our biggest multinational clients.
 The Role 
- Manage multiple client engagements. 
- Contribute to client delivery teams, providing guidance and training to junior team members as needed, and take responsibility for client deliverables 
- Operate on teams providing advice on global health, risk and other benefits. 
- Engage with clients, building relationships and provide consistent, superior project delivery. 
- Manage large International consulting client engagements: 
- Coordinate teams and promote effective working 
- Develop project plans for execution of large, global engagements 
- Ensure project managers are maintaining team progress against goals 
- Build relationships internally and collaborate effectively on cross-functional and cross-regional teams. 
- Partnering with regional/ local Health & Benefits, International consultants and regional/local geography teams 
- Contribute to relationships with internal and external sources to maximize the activity on key target accounts 
 What you’ll bring 
- 3+ years of project management, client facing or consulting experience 
- Employee benefits experience, preferably with health and risk benefits, Rewards or HR expertise (across multiple countries is a bonus) 
- Fluent in English language (Fluency in a Scandinavian language is a bonus). 
- Track record of success in managing client contact relationships, demonstrating ability to communicate clearly in a client-facing role 
- Ability to work both on their own and with client teams, including virtual work teams with members in different geographic locations. 
- Understanding of the nuances of working across borders, with different cultures and with multinational organizations, 
- The ability to deal positively with change and comfort working in a global environment. 
- Strong organizational abilities and flexibility to work in a fast-paced, performance driven environment managing multiple project priorities. 
- Interest and aptitude in keeping abreast of latest developments in global compensation/benefits approaches and contributing to the development of new tools and approaches. 
- The ability to use Microsoft Excel to manipulate and analyze data, as well as a working knowledge of Microsoft PowerPoint

 What You Will Do: 
 At Guidehouse, grants management is not a back-office compliance function—it’s where public dollars turn into real outcomes. Our team works at the center of some of the largest, most complex federal and state funding programs in the country, partnering directly with government leaders to design, launch, and sustain programs that matter—from healthcare access and community recovery to energy transition and infrastructure resilience.
 You’ll join a team that combines deep technical credibility with strategic influence. We don’t just help clients comply with 2 CFR 200—we shape how programs are structured, governed, and delivered so they withstand scrutiny, adapt to shifting federal priorities, and produce measurable impact. Our consultants are trusted advisors, often embedded alongside agency leadership, helping translate policy into executable, audit defensible operations.
 Guidehouse invests in how grants work tomorrow, not just how they worked yesterday. That includes modernizing grants operations with data, analytics, and AI enabled tools—while maintaining the rigor, transparency, and human judgment that public funding demands. You’ll have opportunities to innovate responsibly, build new solutions, and influence firmwide approaches to grants modernization.
 Equally important, you’ll be part of a collaborative, mission driven culture. We value clarity, quality, and professionalism—and we support career paths that reward both subject matter depth and leadership. Whether you want to specialize deeply, lead large programs, or grow into broader advisory roles, Guidehouse provides the platform and trust to do meaningful work at scale.
 If you’re looking for a place where your grants expertise is respected, your ideas shape outcomes, and your work has visible public value, this is that team.
 As a Grants Management Consultant or Senior Consultant, you will support the design and implementation of federal grant projects for state and local government clients. You will support areas such as strategic planning, financial management, monitoring and compliance, and stakeholder engagement to provide full lifecycle grants management support. This role is an exciting opportunity to guide clients through transformative programs and to be a part of an impactful mission.
 Specific responsibilities will include:

- Help to identify and proactively address client needs by presenting potential solutions to challenges or issues 
- Participate in client discussions and meetings 
- Effectively and concisely communicate and present information to clients and leadership 
- Develop agendas, meeting materials, and talking points in preparation for meetings 
- Develop high-quality presentations that effectively communicate key objectives and facilitate discussion across multiple stakeholders 
- Develop and ensure quality deliverables 
- Participate in business development activities

- Participate in internal and external grants management-related training, knowledge management, and thought leadership activities

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills and the ability to interact professionally with a diverse group of executives, managers, and subject matter experts

- Advanced proficiency in the full Microsoft Suite, including MS Teams, PowerPoint, Word, and Excel

En ERM estamos en búsqueda de un/a Consultor/a en Sostenibilidad para integrarse a un equipo dedicado, asignado a un proyecto estratégico de certificación internacional para un operador del sector de hidrocarburos en Argentina. El rol requiere una sólida experiencia técnica en gestión socioambiental y relaciones comunitarias, articulando con diferentes áreas del negocio y aplicando estándares internacionales.
 En ERM, sabemos que crear un entorno de trabajo diverso, equitativo e inclusivo es una parte esencial para hacer de nuestra empresa un excelente lugar para desarrollar una carrera.
 Principales responsabilidades:
- Elaborar, revisar y actualizar reportes técnicos de sostenibilidad y desempeño socioambiental. 
- Recopilar, sistematizar y analizar información e indicadores ESG de distintas áreas. 
- Organizar y mantener la documentación y las evidencias requeridas para procesos de certificación y auditoría. 
- Dar seguimiento a planes de acción, compromisos y requerimientos de información. 
- Apoyar la identificación de brechas frente a estándares internacionales y la preparación de recomendaciones.
 Requisitos: 
- Título universitario en Ingeniería, Ciencias Ambientales, Ciencias Sociales o disciplinas afines. 
- Experiencia en gestión ambiental y social (E&S), criterios ESG y relacionamiento con grupos de interés. 
- Conocimiento de estándares internacionales, incluyendo IFC Performance Standards, Principios de Ecuador y marcos de reporte ESG y sostenibilidad. 
- Disponibilidad para realizar viajes según las necesidades de los proyectos 
 Antecedentes: 
 Desde que establecimos nos establecimos en la región de América Latina y el Caribe (LAC) en la década de 1990, ERM ha crecido de manera constante, empleando ahora a más de 800 profesionales en sus oficinas de Argentina, Brasil, Colombia, Guyana, México y Perú. Durante más de 30 años, hemos construido equipos de consultoría de clase mundial, especializados en medio ambiente, sostenibilidad y consultoría social, con una sólida base de clientes en múltiples sectores económicos como petróleo y gas, manufactura y productos químicos, entre otros. A lo largo de tiempos desafiantes, ERM ha permanecido comprometida en apoyar a estos sectores, ya que nuestros clientes continúan invirtiendo en el mercado local.
 Como parte de nuestra expansión regional, ERM busca mantener el liderazgo en la industria asociándose con importantes clientes que comparten nuestro compromiso con la sostenibilidad. Con una base sólida en industrias clave, somos pioneros en el avance de la agenda ESG (Ambiental, Social y de Gobernanza) en América Latina y el Caribe. Nuestro trabajo incluye contribuir a iniciativas de financiamiento sostenible, desarrollar estudios temáticos y apoyar la implementación de estándares internacionales para las partes interesadas.
 Quiénes Somos: 
 Como la mayor consultora global dedicada exclusivamente a la sostenibilidad, nos asociamos con las principales organizaciones del mundo, creando soluciones innovadoras a los desafíos de sostenibilidad y desbloqueando oportunidades comerciales que satisfacen las necesidades del presente, mientras preservamos oportunidades para las futuras generaciones.
 También consideramos nuestra diversidad como una fortaleza que nos ayuda a crear mejores soluciones para nuestros clientes. Nuestro equipo diverso de expertos de clase mundial apoya a los clientes en todos los niveles de sus organizaciones para operacionalizar la sostenibilidad, respaldado por nuestra profunda experiencia técnica en la resolución de temas ambientales, de salud, seguridad, riesgo y asuntos sociales. Llamamos a esta capacidad nuestro enfoque de "boots to boardroom" un modelo de servicio integral que permite a ERM desarrollar soluciones estratégicas y técnicas que impulsan objetivos tanto en el campo como a nivel ejecutivo.
 Si deseas leer más sobre Diversidad, Equidad, Igualdad e Inclusión (DEIB) en ERM, puedes visitar nuestro sitio web o conocer nuestros avances en el Informe de Sostenibilidad 2026 .

jd_text:
Help Shape More Sustainable, Inclusive, and Resilient Projects Across Communities and Industries 
 ERM is seeking a Consultant, Social Performance (Part-Time) to join our growing team supporting impactful projects in Canada. In this Part-Time role (24 hours/week) , you will work alongside experienced practitioners, clients, Indigenous organizations, governments, and other stakeholders to address complex social, environmental, and economic challenges. From mining and energy to renewables and infrastructure, you will help shape projects that balance business objectives with community needs, social responsibility, and long-term sustainability. This is an opportunity to build a meaningful consulting career while contributing to work that creates positive outcomes for people, communities, and the environment.
 Why This Role Matters 
 As a Consultant, Social Performance, you will play an important role in advancing responsible development across Canada and internationally. Your expertise will help clients navigate social risks, strengthen community relationships, and embed responsible practices into major mining, renewables, infrastructure, and industrial projects. By combining research, stakeholder engagement, and strategic thinking, you will help organizations make informed decisions that generate tangible benefits for communities, Indigenous Nations, stakeholders, and project teams.
 What Your Impact Is 
 In this role, you will support ERM projects and clients to strengthen community and Indigenous engagement and effectively manage social risks and opportunities associated with major capital projects and industrial operations.
 Your work will help clients:
- Make informed decisions through high-quality research, analysis, and communication of complex information. 
- Understand and address social risks, opportunities, and stakeholder concerns. 
- Develop practical strategies that support responsible business practices and project success. 
- Build productive relationships with Indigenous Nations, communities, governments, and other stakeholders. 
- Deliver positive social, environmental, and economic outcomes through effective project execution. Working as part of multidisciplinary teams, you will help develop innovative, actionable solutions to some of the most pressing social challenges facing industry today.
 What You'll Bring 
 Required 
- Post-secondary degree in international development, law, public policy, political science, human rights, geography, public health, economics, social science, resource management, anthropology, or similar. 
- 2+ years of relevant experience, including stakeholder and Indigenous engagement, fieldwork (e.g., interviews, focus groups), impact assessment, environmental and social due diligence, and/or related activities in Canada and/or internationally. 
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills, both written and verbal, demonstrated through clear and respectful interactions with colleagues and clients. 
- Strong time management, prioritization, and organizational skills. 
- Keen attention to detail and the ability to tailor deliverables to the specific needs and audiences of clients and stakeholders. 
- Ability to work collaboratively within a team environment, take direction, and work independently on tasks contributing to broader project outcomes. 
- Ability to conduct research (e.g., web-based research, literature reviews, surveys, and/or interviews), analyze data, and present findings clearly and concisely. 
- Initiative and willingness to take on new responsibilities, support new initiatives, and seek clarification when needed. 
- Critical thinking and strategic problem-solving skills. 
- This position is not eligible for immigration sponsorship. 
 Preferred 
- Master’s degree (or higher) in a relevant field. 
- Experience working with Indigenous Nations or Indigenous organizations in British Columbia and Northern Canada. 
- Experience working with and/or engaging vulnerable populations. 
- Previous consulting experience. 
- Experience synthesizing complex environmental and engineering information into plain-language summaries. 
- Project management skills and experience. 
- Working fluency in a second language (French or Spanish preferred). 
- Driver's License Required: This position requires a valid driver's license and/or the ability to operate a company vehicle due to the nature of job duties, which include frequent travel to various client locations across a large geographical area. 
 Key Responsibilities 
- Support successful consulting engagements through research, analysis, and preparation of project deliverables. 
- Coordinate stakeholder engagement activities, including engagement planning, engagement tracking, and development of engagement materials. 
- Support note-taking and reporting for stakeholder meetings, client meetings, workshops, and engagement sessions. 
- Conduct desktop research and literature reviews to support project delivery and inform the development of baseline studies, impact assessments, engagement plans, management plans, and related materials. 
- Think critically and strategically to help enhance project outcomes and maximize value for clients. 
- Collaborate with colleagues across ERM service areas, contributing expertise while supporting multidisciplinary project teams when needed. 
- Contribute to the ongoing growth, development, and success of ERM’s team, systems, and culture. 
- Contribute to ERM projects and initiatives in Canada and, where applicable, internationally. 
 For the  Consultant, Social Performance (Part-Time, 24 hours/week) position, the anticipated annual base pay is $43,854-$56,584 CAD . Actual pay will depend on factors such as education, experience, skills, location, performance, and business needs. In some cases, pay may fall outside this range. This role may be eligible for bonus pay subject to the sole discretion of ERM and its policies and procedures (casual and fixed term/flex force employees are not bonus eligible).  
 We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including paid time off, parental leave, medical, dental, vision, life, disability, AD&D insurance, RRSP/DPSP, and other applicable benefits to eligible employees.  
 Who We Are: 
 As the largest global pure play sustainability consultancy, we partner with the world’s leading organizations, creating innovative solutions to sustainability challenges and unlocking commercial opportunities that meet the needs of today while preserving opportunity for future generations.
 At ERM we know that creating a diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment is an essential part of making our company a great place to build a career. We also see our diversity as a strength that helps us create better solutions for our clients. Our diverse team of world-class experts supports clients across the breadth of their organizations to operationalize sustainability, underpinned by our deep technical expertise in addressing their environmental, health, safety, risk and social issues. We call this capability our “boots to boardroom” approach for its comprehensive service model that allows ERM to develop strategic and technical solutions that advance objectives on the ground or at the executive level.

 ERM is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, age, Indigenous identity, or status as a protected veteran or qualified individual with a disability.
 ERM does not accept recruiting agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, ERM employees or any other company location. ERM is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

 Responsibilities

- Review contractor submissions and records, including method statements, inspection reports, monitoring results, waste documentation, licences, permits, training records and statutory certificates. 
- Monitor controls for high-risk activities, including work at height, lifting, excavation, confined-space entry, electrical work, hot work, traffic management, mobile plant and simultaneous operations. 
- Monitor environmental controls for erosion and sediment, scheduled wastes, wastewater and effluent, dust, noise, air emissions, chemical storage, spills and sensitive receptors. 
- Record observations and non-conformances, agree corrective actions with the EPCC contractor, and verify close-out within the required timeframe. 
- Support incident notification, investigation and root-cause analysis, and track corrective and preventive actions to closure. 
- Participate in site coordination and EHS meetings, progress reviews and emergency drills; promptly escalate significant, repeated or overdue issues to client site management. 
- Prepare clear daily, weekly and monthly reports covering compliance status, inspection findings, incidents, performance indicators, outstanding actions and emerging risks. 
- Liaise with regulatory authorities when authorised by the client and support inspections, submissions and follow-up actions. 
- Exercise stop-work authority in accordance with project procedures where there is imminent danger, serious non-compliance or unacceptable environmental risk. 
- Maintain complete, current and auditable site EHS records.

- Degree or diploma in environmental science, engineering, occupational safety and health, construction management or a related technical discipline.

- Practical awareness of electrical safety, including temporary installations and distribution boards, isolation and lockout/tagout, energised-work interfaces, earthing, residual-current protection, cable management, portable tools and coordination with authorised electrical personnel. 
- Practical knowledge of construction environmental controls, including scheduled wastes, wastewater, erosion and sediment, dust, noise, chemical storage and spill response.

This Opportunity 
 WSP is currently initiating a search for a Senior Consultant to support our company’s growing Resilience Services Practice. This is a full-time position located in our Miami, Sunrise, Tampa, Jacksonville, or Tallahassee offices in the United States. The position requires you to be physically located in Florida.
 This technical leadership position will lead climate adaptation projects and guide decisions on resilience investments. A significant part of the role involves connecting information between the risk analysis team and the engineering/design team and communicating with clients on risk reduction within infrastructure capital investments. A strong candidate would be well-versed in project management, including client interaction, team management, and project financials.
 This position will also support business development in Florida under local and national leadership. Activities may include presentations at conferences, engagement with professional groups, and other activities. Therefore, openness to learning to be comfortable with public speaking, if not already, is essential.
 The ideal candidate is a self-starter and independent worker, comfortable collaborating virtually with team members, and willing to travel within Florida. The position will be part of the national climate resilience team with team members located across the United States.
 Your Impact 
- You are expected to lead projects/tasks and project teams on topics including project-level risk assessment, adaptation alternatives, preliminary engineering design, and communication. Initially, most projects focus on roadway infrastructure. 
- You will also work closely with our risk analysis and engineering team. Our Resilience Services Practice risk analysis team includes climate scientists, engineers, planners, economists, policy specialists, and risk modelers. Engineering teams include stormwater drainage, coastal, civil, structural, transportation, alternative-delivery (design-build), and others. 
- You will contribute to a diverse team of experts working to advance the Resilience Services Practice through effective data-driven analysis and decision-making. 
- Prepare data and visualizations such as tables, charts, accurate reports, and illustrations for the interpretation or presentation of data, findings, or analyses. 
- Maintain quality control standards and procedures for accurate and precise measurements, statistical analysis, and reporting. 
- Assist with development and scoping of medium-sized projects. 
- Prepare technical reports and presentations that explain research, findings, and recommendations 
- Work with cross-functional teams in executing project work. 
- Comply with regulatory requirements pertaining to the data integrity, documentation, procedures, training, monitoring systems, and record compliance and retention. 
- Interact with regulatory agencies, subcontractors, and clients in a confident and professional manner. 
- Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures. 
- Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs. 
 Who You Are 
 Required Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree or higher in Stormwater, Civil, or Environmental Engineering or a related engineering field 
- 5-8 years of work experience. 
- Experience working on climate change vulnerability, risk assessments, risk reduction strategies/ alternatives. 
- Proven capabilities for technical project delivery and working with interdisciplinary technical teams. 
- Experience working both independently and on efforts requiring collaboration, remotely. 
- Experience communicating technical analysis and results to non-technical audiences. 
- Attention to detail; commitment and skills to identify and detect errors; commitment to thorough quality reviews and checks; and commitment to accuracy, correctness, and excellence. 
- Ability to innovate on challenging topics to produce client-tailored products. 
- Highly capable self-leadership with attention to detail, multi-tasking, and prioritization of responsibilities in a dynamic work environment. 
- Ability to work independently and provide guidance and leadership to junior team or project members, with strict adherence to QA/QC.

jd_text:
What if you could do the kind of work the world needs?​ 
 At WSP, you can access our global scale, contribute to landmark projects and connect with the brightest minds in your field to do the best work of your life. You can embrace your curiosity in a culture that celebrates new ideas and diverse perspectives. You can experience a world of opportunity and the chance to shape a career as unique as you.
 WSP is one of the world's leading engineering and environmental professional services firms providing technical consultancy to the built and natural environment. We believe that for societies to thrive, we must all hold ourselves accountable for tomorrow. For us, that means creating innovative solutions to the challenges the future will bring to the communities and environments where we live and work across the UK. 
 We are locally dedicated and propelled by international brainpower. We are technical experts and strategic advisors, including engineers, technicians, scientists, planners, surveyors, geo-science and environmental specialists, as well as other design, programme and construction management professionals. Our experts influence and design sustainable lasting solutions in the property & buildings, transportation & infrastructure, earth & environment, industry and power & energy sectors as well as project delivery and strategic consulting services. 
 ROLE 
 As Senior Consultant - Future Energy Networks , you will deliver and increasingly lead high-quality consulting projects and workstreams that help network operators, utilities and other energy-sector clients plan, transform and future-proof energy systems. Future Energy Networks is part of WSP's wider integrated Energy Advisory business, which brings together four core capabilities:
- Markets Advisory – helping clients understand how energy markets operate, how market arrangements evolve, and how commercial value is created.
- Policy & Regulation – supporting governments, regulators, system operators and utilities with policy development, economic regulation and regulatory reform.
- Energy Decarbonisation – helping organisations, cities, utilities and governments secure, plan and optimise energy in an increasingly electrified economy.
- Future Energy Networks – supporting network operators and utilities to plan, transform, deliver and future-proof the energy systems of the future.
 Energy Advisory operates as a single integrated business, and all consultants are encouraged to contribute across multiple capabilities. This provides opportunities to broaden technical and consulting skills, work on multidisciplinary projects and develop a deeper understanding of the energy transition.
 Working alongside engineers, economists, policy specialists, strategists and commercial advisors, you will deliver projects and increasingly lead defined workstreams across areas such as network planning, connections, flexibility, network transformation and innovation. You will engage directly with clients, apply sound analysis and judgement, and take ownership of clear, practical and high-quality outputs.
 You will contribute to the development of Future Energy Networks and the wider Energy Advisory business through knowledge sharing, business development and the improvement of our services and ways of working. We are looking for relevant experience in one or more areas, strong consulting or delivery skills, and the curiosity and potential to develop across the wider Future Energy Networks agenda.
 RESPONSIBILITIES 
- Delivering consulting projects and defined workstreams, with increasing responsibility for planning, coordination and successful outcomes.
- Taking ownership of high-quality project outputs, including technical accuracy, clear communication, timely delivery and effective use of project resources.
- Applying relevant experience to challenges in network planning, connections, flexibility, network transformation, innovation and related areas of the energy transition.
- Developing proportionate analytical approaches, work plans and recommendations in response to client requirements.
- Engaging directly with client stakeholders, presenting findings clearly and building trusted working relationships.
- Working effectively in multidisciplinary teams and, where appropriate, coordinating colleagues and supporting their development.
- Delivering technical, commercial, economic, policy and strategic analysis to support client decision-making.
- Contributing to business cases, regulatory submissions, market assessments, network or energy strategies and implementation plans.
- Identifying practical improvements to tools, methods and approaches that strengthen project delivery and WSP's advisory capability.
- Contributing to proposals, bids, client development and other business development activities.
- Supporting the development of Future Energy Networks services, market offerings and team capability.
- Sharing knowledge and, where relevant, contributing to publications, events and wider industry engagement.
 KEY COMPETENCIES AND EXPERIENCE 
- Relevant experience gained in consulting, electricity networks, utilities or the wider energy sector.
- Experience contributing to the delivery of consulting, advisory, technical or strategic projects, with evidence of increasing responsibility for projects or workstreams.
- Knowledge or experience in one or more areas such as network planning, connections, flexibility, network transformation, innovation, resilience or energy-system planning.
- Ability to work effectively in complex or evolving environments, using sound judgement and seeking support where appropriate.
- Experience engaging directly with clients or other stakeholders and translating their needs into clear, practical outputs.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving and critical-thinking skills.
- Ability to communicate complex topics clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, both in writing and verbally.
- Effective stakeholder engagement and relationship-building skills.
- Good commercial awareness, including an understanding of project delivery, client value and the role of business development.
- Experience supporting, mentoring or sharing knowledge with colleagues, or a willingness to develop these skills.
- Ability to collaborate across disciplines and contribute constructively to team and capability development.
- A willingness and ability to contribute across the wider Energy Advisory business beyond your primary area of experience.
 QUALIFICATIONS 
- A degree or equivalent relevant experience in an engineering, scientific, technical, economic, policy or related discipline.
- Chartered status, or progress towards professional accreditation with a relevant body, is desirable but not essential.
 Imagine a better future for you and a better future for us all. 
 Join our close-knit community of talented individuals who share your passion for making a positive impact. Our global team includes more than 69,000 employees, working together to make a difference in communities both close to home and around the world.
 With us, you can.

 You will be responsible for delivering larger and/or more complex components of projects, applying knowledge of a defined capability area (e.g. organisational development, culture & change, leadership, team effectiveness) and applying structured, evidence-based analysis to diagnose organisational challenges and derive actionable insights.  At Arup, you belong to an extraordinary collective – in which we encourage individuality to thrive. - Leadership & capability.

jd_text:
Joining Arup 
 Arup’s purpose, shared values and collaborative approach has set us apart for over 80 years, guiding how we shape a better world.
 The Opportunity 
 The Sustainability team within Arup’s Property London division works with a range of property clients to develop and deliver sustainability and carbon strategies for property development and refurbishment projects, both independently and as part of multi-disciplinary Arup teams. Increasingly the brief for these developments includes an aspiration to achieve Net Zero Carbon, and so energy performance is a key focus.
 We are seeking an energy modelling consultant to join the growing energy modelling group within the sustainability team. This group provides some oversight of general IES modelling for Part L compliance, but is primarily focused on advanced energy modelling, including for TM54, NABERS and LEED, as well as early stage parametric modelling using tools such as Grasshopper. In addition to delivering more advanced energy modelling, this core team is responsible for training and skills development for engineers working in these areas.
 The successful candidate for this role will be responsible for delivery of advanced energy modelling across a number of projects, including both undertaking modelling directly and guiding graduates and apprentices in the development of IES models. We are able to support the successful candidate through their Chartership journey.
 The role will include: 
 · Undertaking advanced energy modelling including for TM54, NABERS and bespoke project requirements, using a combination of IES-VE, including APACHE HVAC, spreadsheets and other advanced analytics tools as needed. 
 · Oversee junior engineers/modellers in the delivery of advanced energy modelling. 
 · Engage with project mechanical designers to ensure the energy model is a close representation of the design, and that the modelling outcomes inform the design development. 
 · Review/assist junior engineers in the delivery of Part L energy /compliance models. 
 · Contribute to the development of training resources and the delivery of advanced energy modelling training for our engineers. 
 · Contribute to the delivery of research focused on improving the tools, techniques and approaches we employ for advanced energy modelling. 
 · The role will be based in Central London but may involve some travel l ing nationally and internationally. 
 At Arup, you belong to an extraordinary collective – in which we encourage individuality to thrive. Our strength comes from how we respect, share and connect our diverse experiences, perspectives and ideas.
 You will have the opportunity do socially useful work that has meaning – to Arup, to your career, to our members and to the clients and communities we serve.
 Is this role right for you? 
 · At least 2 years using IES VE with ApacheHVAC for advanced modelling (TM54 or NABERS or LEED) as a major part of current or previous role.
 · Proven experience in undertaking a range of energy modelling activities or a range of project types such as energy performance modelling, compliance and thermal comfort analysis, including models for planning and as-built (Part L, EPCs), familiarity with Building Regulations Part L.
 · Experience/awareness of TM54 / BREEAM Ene01 / NABERS UK and/or LEED.
 · Experience in Data Analysis using Excel.
 · Developing understanding of building HVAC systems and controls.
 · Degree in an area such as; mechanical engineering, building services, architectural engineering, building physics.
 · Working towards chartership with CIBSE, IMechE or other relevant Engineering Council body.
 · Holds or interested to obtain qualifications as Low Carbon Consultant, Low Carbon Energy Assessor, Non-domestic Energy Assessor.
 · Experience/ interest in SAP and domestic energy assessment is of interest.
 · Participates in industry bodies/conferences related to energy modelling, building performance, Net Zero and other topics related to the sustainability of the built environment.
 · Able to work autonomously, stay focused and with attention to detail.
 · Experience of working in multi-disciplinary teams.
 · Ability to work under pressure and meet strict deadlines.
 · Excellent communication skills (both written and oral).
 · Excellent planning, organisational and time management skills.
 · Highly motivated and willing to take on new challenges.
 The following skills are not essential but would be beneficial to the delivery of the role:
 · Experience with another package such as DesignBuilder or EDSL TAS is a bonus.
 · Experience in parametric energy and thermal modelling using Grasshopper, Ladybug and Honeybee.
 · Coding experience (Python, Visual Basic etc.).
 · Ability to work 3D/3D CAD software i.e. AutoCAD, Sketchup, Rhino and Revit etc. 
 What we offer you 
 At Arup, we care about each member’s success, so we can grow together. Guided by our values, we provide an attractive total reward package that recognises the contribution of each of our members to our shared success. As well as competitive, fair and equitable pay, we offer a career in which all of our members can belong, grow and thrive – through benefits that support health and wellbeing, a wide range of learning opportunities and many possibilities to have an impact through the work they do.
 We are owned in trust on behalf of our members, giving us the freedom, with personal responsibility, to set our own direction and choose work that aligns with our purpose and adds to Arup’s legacy. Our members collaborate on ambitious projects to deliver remarkable outcomes for our clients and communities. Profit Share is a key part of our reward, enabling members to share in the results of our collective efforts.
 We also provide Private medical insurance, Life assurance, Accident insurance and Income protection cover. In addition, you’ll have access to flexible benefits to help you look after all aspects of your wellbeing and give you the freedom and flexibility to find the best solutions for you, your family, and your individual needs.
 Different people, shared values 
 Arup is an equal opportunity employer that actively promotes and nurtures a diverse and inclusive workforce. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of age (within legal limits), gender identity or expression, marital status, disability, neurotype or mental health, race or ethnicity, faith or belief, sexual orientation, socioeconomic background, and whether you’re pregnant or on family leave. We are an open environment that embraces diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas – this drives our excellence. 
 Guided by our values and alignment with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, we create and contribute to equitable spaces and systems, while cultivating a sense of belonging for all. Our internal employee networks support our inclusive culture: from race, ethnicity and cross-cultural working to gender equity and LGBTQ+ and disability inclusion – we aim to create a space for you to express yourself and make a positive difference. Discover more about life at Arup at www.arup.com/careers/your-life-at-arup.
 We are committed to making our recruitment process and workplaces accessible to all candidates. Please contact us to let us know if you need any assistance or reasonable adjustments throughout your application or interview process, and/or to perform the essential functions of the role. We will do everything we can to support you.
 Our Application Process 
 To understand what to expect next, please visit https://www.arup.com/careers/recruitment-process/
 Stay safe online – Arup will never ask for your bank details as part of our recruitment process.
 Recruitment Agencies - We have a Preferred Supplier List of trusted partners to assist us when required and do not acknowledge any speculative CVs or unsolicited candidate introductions from agencies not on the list.
 We will close the role when we receive a large number of applications, so please ensure you apply early.

summary:
Arup’s purpose, shared values and collaborative approach has set us apart for over 80 years, guiding how we shape a better world.
Dedicated to sustainable development, Arup is a collective of advisors and experts working across 140 countries. Founded to be both humane and excellent, we collaborate with our clients and partners using imagination, technology and rigour to shape a better world.
Our award-winning global transaction advisory team is growing, and we are looking for a consultant to deliver technical advisory assignments to support clients investing in renewables and storage assets and companies.
education: Relevant engineering or environmental related degree, or equivalent experience with renewable energy technologies.
jd_text:
Shape a future with purpose at Arup in Milan. 
 Arup’s purpose, shared values and collaborative approach has set us apart for over 80 years, guiding how we shape a better world. 
 Dedicated to sustainable development, Arup is a collective of advisors and experts working across 140 countries. Founded to be both humane and excellent, we collaborate with our clients and partners using imagination, technology and rigour to shape a better world. 
 Our award-winning global transaction advisory team is growing, and we are looking for a consultant to deliver technical advisory assignments to support clients investing in renewables and storage assets and companies. 
 The Opportunity 
 We are looking for people with project development, operation, engineering, commercial or transaction experience on a range of technologies, including solar, wind, BESS and energy transition. 
 The focus of due diligence work is to help evaluate potential investments by identifying and assessing technical, operational, commercial and reputational risks and opportunities. 
 As a Consultant at Arup, you will: 
- Work on discrete projects, typically consisting of technical, ESG or commercial due diligence, to inform buyers or sellers of assets and companies in the energy transition space. 
- Conduct wider advisory work to support clients navigating the energy transition, in accordance with the individual’s skillsets. 
 Other activities may include: 
- Contributing to project management tasks 
- Taking part to research and analysis assignments. 
- Contributing to bid development for due diligence assignments. 
- Taking part to conversations with clients. 
- Contributing to sectoral knowledge through data analysis. 
- Process improvement and continuous development. 
 Does this role inspire you? 
- We're looking for someone who is passionate about renewable energy advisory services. We also value: 
- Relevant engineering or environmental related degree, or equivalent experience with renewable energy technologies. 
- At least 1-2 years of professional experience in solar, wind, BESS or hybrid systems . 
- Experience in other European markets beside Italy will be appreciated. 
- Any prior experience of undertaking technical due diligence services on energy infrastructure assets. 
- Fluency in both written and spoken English, you have quantitative and analytical skills, and good knowledge of both Excel and PowerPoint. 
 Why Arup? 
 At Arup, we believe in rewarding our members for their contributions to our shared success. As a trust-owned company, we have the freedom to pursue meaningful work that aligns with our purpose and values. We also offer a unique profit share program, allowing our members to share in the results of our collective efforts. 
 Benefits that work for you: 
- Professional Growth & Development: Benefit from continuous learning opportunities, training programs, and mentorship to enhance your skills and advance your career at Arup. 
- Global Opportunities: Collaborate with colleagues worldwide and explore potential short-term or long-term assignments at other Arup offices and project locations. 
- Financial Well-being & Ownership: Receive a competitive salary and benefits package and share in Arup's success through our global profit-sharing programme. 
- Flexible Working: Possibility to work from home for part of the week. 
 At Arup, you belong to an extraordinary collective where individuality is encouraged. Our strength comes from how we respect, share, and connect our diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas. You'll have the opportunity to do socially useful work that has meaning – to Arup, to your career, and to the clients and communities we serve. 
 We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a workplace that reflects the rich diversity of the world around us. We actively promote a culture of inclusion where everyone feels welcome, respected, and valued. 
 We welcome applications from talented individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of age (within legal limits), gender identity or expression, disability, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic. We are committed to making our recruitment process and workplaces accessible. If you need any assistance or adjustments, please visit our Candidate Support page for contact information and assistance. We're happy to help. 
 Do you want to join us in shaping a better world? 
 The gross annual salary (RAL) for this role is €29,500 to €34,000, in accordance with the applicable provisions of the CCNL Terziario (Confcommercio). The final salary is determined using objective and gender-neutral criteria, reflecting experience, qualifications and role-relevant skills.

Joining Arup 
 Arup’s purpose, shared values and collaborative approach has set us apart for 80 years, guiding how we shape a better world.
 Arup is an independent firm of designers, planners, engineers, consultants and technical specialists offering a broad range of professional services. Through our work, we make a positive difference in the world.
 Arup's innovative approach to environmental & sustainability consulting enables clients to achieve their sustainable business and corporate responsibility aspirations. We advise at each stage of a project or business development. Arup offers a multidisciplinary service aimed at developing policy, assessing impact, creative design and implementation, gaining regulatory approvals, reporting publicly, managing risk and controlling costs.
 The Opportunity 
 We are seeking an energetic and enthusiastic Senior Sustainability Consultant with design and/or construction delivery project knowledge. The role involves preparing and delivering sustainability strategies and identifying and managing the implementation of environmental and sustainability measures in projects during design, procurement, construction and/or operation stages.
 The position is for a Senior Consultant to work within our Environment, Climate and Sustainability Services portfolio in London. You will promote and manage a range of projects in the areas of environmental / sustainability advice on significant design and construction projects. Activities will include guiding strategic sustainability advice including leading sustainability strategies, frameworks and appraisals, and auditing of design / construction contractors, ISO 14001, consultation with statutory authorities. The clients will include major infrastructure schemes and private developers. You will be working in a multi-disciplinary environment alongside other environmental, planning, engineering and urban design specialists.
 Your remit will be to undertake and manage the production of technical work, co-ordinate with specialists and multi-disciplinary project teams, be accountable for quality and budget control, and assist with proposal preparation and marketing activities.
 Work as the environmental sustainability representative in project delivery teams to drive and embed aspects of sustainability into major infrastructure and planning projects.
 Develop comprehensive environmental and sustainability strategies and recommendations to project delivery teams and Clients.
 Manage and prepare environmental and sustainability deliverables, coordinating with virtual teams of topic specialists as necessary.
 Prepare and deliver presentations, workshops and/or training to teams and clients. Assist with managing projects including preparing and tracking budgets, resources and programmes
 At Arup, you belong to an extraordinary collective – in which we encourage individuality to thrive. Our strength comes from how we respect, share, and connect our diverse experiences, perspectives and ideas.
 You will have the opportunity do socially useful work that has meaning – to Arup, to your career, to our members and to the clients and communities we serve.
 Is this role right for you? 
 We are looking for people with the following skills –
 · Bachelor’s or Master’s university degree in a relevant field such as Sustainability, Climate Change, Environmental Engineering/Management or Geography. We would prefer qualifications which demonstrate multi-disciplinary and strategic problem solving. Other relevant qualifications will be considered. 
 · Practitioner or Full Member of the Institute of Sustainability and Environmental Professionals (ISEP) or equivalent.
 · Chartered or working towards Chartered Environmentalist.
 · ISEP Registered Environmental Auditor would be an advantage.
 · Qualified or desire to become a qualified BREEAM Infrastructure Project Assessor.
 · Knowledge in delivering environmental sustainability aspects of strategy, design and construction major infrastructure or master planning projects.
 · Appreciation of the principles of environmental sustainability and its relationship to the planning, design and operation of the built environment, including legislation in the UK and Environmental Impact Assessment in a planning context. Writing, editing and reviewing technical and non-technical reports relating to environment and sustainability topics.
 · Awareness of PAS2080 carbon management in infrastructure or similar.
 Not ready to apply just yet, or have some questions? Please email Lei Padua at Lei.Padua@arup.com . Please note, to ensure we remain GDPR compliant do not send your CV directly to us via this email.
 What we offer you
